'''Landing at Taizel''' (Japanese: {{hl|上陸タイゼル港|Jouriku taizeru minato}} ''Landing at Port Taizel'') is the twelfth chapter of [[Ephraim]]'s route in {{FE8}}.

It is not possible to return to the [[world map]] during this chapter.

==Plot==
{{main|Landing at Taizel/Script}}

[[Ephraim]] and his army arrive at [[Taizel]], and find no enemy troops. At the same time, [[Saleh]] escorts [[Ewan]] to Taizel; Ewan explains that [[Marisa]], an associate of his, was accidentally assigned the wrong job, and he wishes to inform her—Saleh then leaves to report his inability to find the "Lord Dragon" to his village. On their ship, Ephraim and [[Seth]] disagree on tactics proceeding into Grado; Seth suggests they use their rear guard to help the front line, but Ephraim refuses to abandon their supply convoy in enemy territory. Ephraim then notices [[Myrrh]] trying to say something, but she decides against speaking up. Just then, enemy forces emerge around the city, and Ephraim prepares for battle.

During the battle, [[Caellach]] orders the Grado soldiers forward, reminding them of the losses of Fort Rigwald and General [[Duessel]]. [[Riev]] then arrives, and informs Caellach that Eirika is traveling to [[Jehanna]], where Caellach was ordered to be. Riev takes Caellach back to Grado Keep, and bolsters Grado's forces with [[monster]]s.

A member of Ephraim's army can visit the lone village, where Ewan is searching for Marisa; Ewan asks for help finding her, and offers to help in battle in exchange. Ewan can talk to Marisa; he informs her that she has been assigned to the wrong job, that her commander [[Gerik]] is working east. Ewan suggests Marisa join Ephraim's army with him, as they are headed east, and Marisa agrees.

After the battle, Ephraim's army prepares to rest in the city. Unbeknownst to Ephraim, Myrrh travels east alone. The next morning, Seth informs Ephraim that Myrrh is missing and was likely sighted heading east. Ephraim orders the army to move east, but Seth hesitates; Ephraim assure him that they would be heading east anyway, and explains that he wishes to retain his compassion when he becomes king. The army then travels east.

==Strategy==
{{strategy}}
{{sectstub}}
This level contains no pressure to move forward or complete it quickly: No enemy will destroy the village that [[Ewan]] is recruited at, Marisa will stand still until you enter her range, the boss doesn't move at all, and the [[Gargoyle]]s that spawn at the end of turn 1 are the only reinforcements that don't cleanly spawn on the enemy side of the map's many chokepoints. Thus the player can just stay on the docks, or even the ship, and let the aggressive enemies kill themselves before moving forward at their leisure. The mix of enemies of the right ship are the main concern due to their aggression and being bunched up with a mix of ranged physical attackers and mages, but each of them presents little threat on their own.

Marisa will attack units that enter her range, and overlaps in range with the adjacent Fighter, but will stay still otherwise. She's not a major threat to most units by this point, but is liable to die on a counter attack. The most straight-forward way to avoid this is to remove the other enemies around her, then lure her out with a bulky unit that has no weapons to counter attack with by trading their weapons away or putting them in the convoy before entering her range.

*The inn that appears in this chapter was originally called a bar in the Japanese version.
